title: Value of a client_secret field in a Zendesk OAuth token request
summary: A synthetic value of client_secret beside client_id in a raw form-encoded token request, a JSON body and a curl -d argument.
rationale: The field is the carrier: Zendesk documents the Secret of an OAuth client as client_secret in API requests, shown once, beside the Identifier used as client_id. Zendesk states no format for the secret, so the value is flagged because of the field it sits in, not because of its shape. The extent is the value only, and the client_id beside it is a public identifier. A public client uses PKCE and sends no client_secret.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: a value in the client_secret field of a token request is treated as a credential whatever its shape. Zendesk documents client_secret in token requests (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and a generic attribution are the project's decisions. No subtype is inferred, and no prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

sources.supports: Identifier: Used as client_id in API requests. Secret: Used as client_secret in API requests. This is shown only once after saving, so store it safely.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
